How we can help

  • Mediation: a calm, structured process for resolving landlord–tenant, family, property, business, and organizational disputes — addressing the emotional and practical dimensions, not just the legal ones.
  • Arbitration: a private alternative to trial when parties can't agree — a neutral arbitrator hears both sides and issues a decision, led by a FINRA arbitrator with extensive arbitration experience.
  • Conflict coaching: one-on-one preparation for a difficult conversation, negotiation, or workplace situation — with a clear strategy, calmer delivery, and realistic goals.
  • Neutral conflict analysis: an impartial review of a recurring dispute in a business, congregation, or organization — identifying root causes and practical next steps.

Four ways to resolve conflict — without litigation

Every matter starts with a free, confidential phone conversation to determine which process fits your situation.

01

Mediation

A neutral mediator facilitates negotiation between the parties so you — not a judge — control the outcome. Voluntary, confidential, and far faster and less expensive than court.

  • Joint and private sessions, in person or virtual
  • Written settlement agreement when you reach terms
  • Best when the relationship matters
02

Arbitration

When parties can't agree but still want to avoid court, a neutral arbitrator hears both sides and issues a decision. Led by a FINRA arbitrator with extensive arbitration experience.

  • Private alternative to a trial
  • Streamlined evidence and hearings, held in person or remotely
  • Binding or non-binding, per your agreement
03

Conflict Coaching

One-on-one coaching that helps you prepare for a difficult conversation, negotiation, or workplace situation — with a clear strategy, calmer delivery, and realistic goals.

  • For individuals, managers, and HR leaders
  • Practical scripts and preparation, not theory
  • Single sessions or a short series
04

Neutral Conflict Analysis

An impartial review of a recurring dispute or strained workplace, congregation, or organization — identifying the root causes and the systemic issues underneath, with practical recommendations.

  • Confidential interviews and document review
  • Findings presented in plain language
  • Suited to businesses, churches, and nonprofits

Church

Leadership, member, and ministry conflicts handled with discretion and care.

Nonprofit

Board, staff, volunteer, and mission-related organizational disputes.

From first call to signed agreement

1

Free intake call

Call (562) 676-1369. You'll describe the dispute, ask questions, and learn whether mediation fits — no obligation.

2

Agreement to mediate

All parties agree to the process, fees, and ground rules in writing. Confidentiality applies from the very first conversation.

3

Virtual or in-person session

Meet in person, or by secure video or phone. The mediator structures the conversation, keeps it productive, and meets privately with each side as needed.

4

Written resolution

Agreements reached are put in writing so everyone leaves with clear, workable terms — often in days or weeks, not months or years.

Mediation with Beama Dispute Resolution Center

  • You keep control of the outcome
  • Private and confidential
  • Typically resolved in days to weeks
  • A fraction of the cost of litigation
  • Preserves working and family relationships

Going to court

  • A judge decides for you
  • Public record
  • Often months to years
  • Attorney fees, filing fees, and time away from work
  • Win–lose outcome that often strains relationships further

Mediation that meets you where you are

Beama Dispute Resolution Center offers both virtual and in-person mediation. Join by secure video or phone from anywhere, or meet in person — whichever works best for your situation. In-person sessions are held at 6740 Sunset Road in Joshua Tree — please call ahead to schedule your appointment.

  • Sessions also available by secure video conference or phone

Meet Rebecca Akumbu

Experience
Mediation & arbitration experience · Practicing since 2019

Rebecca Akumbu founded her dispute resolution practice in 2019 — formerly Akumbu & Associates Disputes Resolution Center, now Beama Dispute Resolution Center — on a simple conviction: most disputes don't need a winner and a loser. They need a skilled neutral, a structured conversation, and terms both sides can actually live with.

Her approach is even-handed and practical. She is known for careful conflict analysis — listening for the interests underneath the positions, naming the real issues plainly, and keeping parties focused on a resolution they design themselves rather than one imposed on them.

Alongside her mediation practice, Rebecca brings years of healthcare claims experience — claims analysis, denials, appeals, and policy interpretation — which gives her a working insider's understanding of healthcare and insurance-related disputes that many mediators simply don't have.

  • USC Master's degree in Alternative Dispute Resolution
  • Yaoundé Master's degree in International Law, University of Yaoundé, Cameroon
  • FINRA Roster arbitrator for financial-industry disputes
  • SCMA–KMC Served on the Board of Directors

Frequently asked questions

Yes. Rebecca Akumbu conducts mediations in person at 6740 Sunset Road, Joshua Tree, CA, and online by secure video or phone — for individuals, families, businesses, and organizations, wherever they are located.
Mediation itself is a voluntary process — nothing is imposed on you. But when parties reach an agreement and put it in a signed written settlement, that agreement is a contract and is enforceable like one. Many mediated agreements can also be entered with the court if a case is already filed.
That's very common — and not a dead end. Call first. In many cases, once the other party receives a professional, neutral invitation explaining the cost and risk of court, they agree to try. The initial conversation about your options is free.
Yes. Mediation is a confidential process. What is discussed in mediation — including in private sessions with the mediator — is not shared with the other side without your permission, and mediation communications are protected under California law.
Fees depend on the type and complexity of the matter and are confirmed in writing before any session is scheduled — no surprises. In nearly every case, the total cost of mediation is a small fraction of what litigation would cost both sides. Call (562) 676-1369 for a quote for your situation.
No. Many clients mediate without attorneys, and you are welcome to have your attorney participate or review an agreement before signing. A mediator is a neutral facilitator, not your lawyer, and does not provide legal advice to either side.
Yes. Your first consultation is free — call (562) 676-1369. Sessions are available in person and virtually, by secure video conference or phone. In-person sessions are held at 6740 Sunset Road, Joshua Tree, CA — please call ahead to schedule your appointment.
